requirement:
Every source text the harness supplies to a model, including mandatory inputs,
`habeas` reads, and `ripgrep` results, and every source text Habeas displays in
the book or `habeas info`, MUST be redacted:

1. In a workspace `habeas.toml` or user configuration file, the value of every
   explicit credential field defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.credentials`
   MUST be replaced. Such a file that is not valid TOML MUST be replaced whole,
   with `configuration` as the kind, because its fields cannot be located.
2. In every source, each match of a built-in rule of the `secretshape` crate MUST
   be replaced. The replaced region MUST be extended through each adjacent region
   that the crate's entropy heuristic flags and that only whitespace separates
   from the region, repeating until no flagged region is adjacent. The heuristic
   MUST NOT cause redaction on its own.

A replacement MUST read `[REDACTED:<kind>]`, where `<kind>` is the credential
field or the rule's name, and MUST keep every line break within the replaced
text, so line numbers are unchanged. Outlines MUST be built from the original
source, and the structural hash MUST hash each text piece that overlaps a
redacted region in its redacted form, so evidence never depends on a credential's
value and redaction never changes or breaks a file's outline. The `secretshape` version MUST be pinned exactly; upgrading
it MAY change redaction and hashes and MUST be treated as a deliberate change.
rationale:
I found no gap in `requirements.authoring.redaction`. I checked the {impl} items and their tests, and read the source-text paths in `src/inputs.rs`, `src/outline/mod.rs` and `src/index.rs` directly. I did not open the ripgrep or `habeas` tool code in `src/authoring/tools.rs`. For those I relied on the test `model_inputs_reads_searches_and_citation_prompts_are_redacted` and on the fact that tool results are built from `node_range`. I did not read `src/redaction/tests.rs` outside the inputs given.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Credential fields in a workspace `habeas.toml` or the user configuration file.**
  - `credential_fields`, `item_fields` and `value_fields` in `src/redaction.rs` redact every leaf value under an authoring configuration's `credentials` and its `api_key`. They also handle inline tables.
  - `is_configuration_file` and `is_configuration_file_for` recognise any file named `habeas.toml`, the user configuration file, and aliases of it.
  - `Redaction::of_file` adds these regions on top of the `secretshape` regions.
- **Invalid TOML replaced whole, with kind `configuration`.** `configuration_regions` returns `0..len` with kind `configuration` when `credential_fields` returns `None`.
- **`secretshape` rule matches replaced.** `secret_regions` and `scanners` use rule-only scanning with the input cap removed.
- **Extension through whitespace-adjacent heuristic regions, never starting a region.**
  - `secret_regions` starts from rule findings only. It then extends each region forward and backward over flagged spans that are adjacent or separated only by whitespace.
  - Heuristic findings alone never start a region.
  - `merge` joins regions that overlap after extension.
- **Replacement reads `[REDACTED:<kind>]` and keeps line breaks.** `Redaction::slice`, `apply` and `push_line_breaks` emit the marker once per region and keep every `\n`, including `\r\n` pairs. `redact_lines` keeps the line count.
- **Outlines built from the original source; pieces hashed in redacted form.**
  - `parse_redacted` parses the original source. `Builder::piece` and `encode` hash `redaction.slice(...)`. `plain_text` hashes the redacted line.
  - `OutlineCache::parse` builds the outline from the original and keeps a separate redacted copy for display.
- **`secretshape` pinned exactly.** `Cargo.toml` has `secretshape = "=0.1.0"`, with a comment saying a new version may change redaction and hashes.
- **Every source text supplied to a model or displayed is redacted.**
  - Mandatory inputs and `habeas` reads go through `InputSelector::resolve` and `node_range`, which use redacted text. The same path serves ripgrep and ast_grep results.
  - Declaration text goes through `redact_lines`.
  - Citation commentary goes through `model_citations_value`. Violation text in site prompts goes through `matches_value`. GitHub issue title and body go through `fetch`.
  - `habeas info` and the book go through `render_detail_sections` and `render_input`. These redact the definition text, validation findings, unresolved raw JSON, unreadable records, and input text.

**Tests**
- `src/redaction/tests.rs` covers:
  - credential fields by name, including inline tables and non-configuration `.toml` files;
  - private-key blocks and CRLF;
  - rule matches without adjacent code;
  - heuristic-only findings not being redacted;
  - hashes not depending on credential values;
  - redaction never changing an outline's structure;
  - slices concatenating to the redacted whole;
  - invalid configuration files redacted whole;
  - the user configuration file and its aliases;
  - backward extension and scanning past 1 MiB.
- `model_inputs_reads_searches_and_citation_prompts_are_redacted` in `src/authoring/tools.rs` covers mandatory inputs, prompts, `habeas` reads, ripgrep results and citation commentary.
- The ast_grep test, `violation_text_reaches_the_model_redacted` in `src/sites.rs`, `the_tool_reads_issues_with_the_token_and_redacts_bodies` in `src/github.rs`, and `detail_pages_and_info_display_redacted_source` in `src/index.rs` cover the remaining paths.
- The version pin is a declaration with no conditional, so it needs no test.

**Marking.** I found no unmarked implementing code and no unmarked tests among the sources I read.

**Possible gap, not reported.** `FIXME` entries in the detail page are escaped but not run through `redact_text`. They are validated to match the `{fixme}` body text exactly, so I did not count this as a gap against the requirement's text.

text: :::{req} redaction
Every source text the harness supplies to a model, including mandatory inputs,
`habeas` reads, and `ripgrep` results, and every source text Habeas displays in
the book or `habeas info`, MUST be redacted:
1. In a workspace `habeas.toml` or user configuration file, the value of every
explicit credential field defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.credentials`
MUST be replaced. Such a file that is not valid TOML MUST be replaced whole,
with `configuration` as the kind, because its fields cannot be located.
2. In every source, each match of a built-in rule of the `secretshape` crate MUST
be replaced. The replaced region MUST be extended through each adjacent region
that the crate's entropy heuristic flags and that only whitespace separates
from the region, repeating until no flagged region is adjacent. The heuristic
MUST NOT cause redaction on its own.
A replacement MUST read `[REDACTED:<kind>]`, where `<kind>` is the credential
field or the rule's name, and MUST keep every line break within the replaced
text, so line numbers are unchanged. Outlines MUST be built from the original
source, and the structural hash MUST hash each text piece that overlaps a
redacted region in its redacted form, so evidence never depends on a credential's
value and redaction never changes or breaks a file's outline. The `secretshape` version MUST be pinned exactly; upgrading
it MAY change redaction and hashes and MUST be treated as a deliberate change.
:::{req} credentials
Bedrock configurations MAY supply `credentials` containing nonempty
`access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, and optional nonempty `session_token`.
Ollama configurations MAY supply a nonempty `api_key`. Habeas MUST reject a
Bedrock record combining explicit credentials with `aws_profile`, and an Ollama
record combining `api_key` with `api_key_env`.
Explicit credentials MUST be passed directly to the selected provider without
changing process environment variables or writing credential files. Saved
explicit values MUST round-trip; credentials resolved from profiles or the
environment MUST NOT be serialized back. Debug output, configuration diagnostics,
usage records, and initial prompts MUST NOT include credential values. TOML
diagnostics MUST NOT echo credential-containing source lines. A configuration
file containing explicit credentials MAY be read as source; its credential
values MUST be redacted under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`.
Validation MUST report a workspace `habeas.toml` present in the Git index that
contains explicit credentials, naming the file and the credential fields and
recommending credential-source references, because committed credentials leak.
Documentation MUST discourage literal credentials in workspace files and
recommend AWS profiles or environment-variable references. Examples MUST use
placeholders and explain that workspace files may be committed or read as source
when explicitly allowed.
